A good bar fight waiting to happen!|GT-9R and Tirog|<ref name="Second Edition">[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'', Second Edition]]</ref>}}
The '''Dancing Dewback''' was a [[Cantina/Legends|cantina]] with a mostly non-[[Human/Legends|Human]] clientele which operated during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. The [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] [[GT-9R]] visited the cantina on two recorded occasions: once while accompanying his master, a [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] named [[Tirog]]; and once with the outlaw [[Dirk Harkness]], a [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] named [[Rhen]], a child named [[Cev Rees]], and a bounty hunter called [[Thannik]].

==Description==
[[File:Dancing_Dewback_map.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Sketch of the Dancing Dewback floor plan, during [[Thannik]]'s meeting with a [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] seated as indicated.]]
The Dancing Dewback's dimly-lit main room was roughly square-shaped, with a floor space of about twenty square [[Meter/Legends|meters]]. There were fifteen booths and nine additional floor tables, plus seating at a large U-shaped bar extending from one wall to the center of the room. The main entrance was directly across from the bar.<ref name="Revised and Expanded">''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref>

The Dancing Dewback had a mainly non-[[Human/Legends|Human]] clientele.<ref name="Second Edition" /> [[Smuggler/Legends|Smugglers]], [[Gambler/Legends|gamblers]], and [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] were among its customers. To a seasoned traveler used to an adventurous lifestyle, the potential for violence was apparent.<ref name="Revised and Expanded" /><ref name="Second Edition" />

A drink of [[Lum/Legends|lum]] at the bar cost two [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]].<ref name="Revised and Expanded" /> Another beverage on offer glowed red, with an apparent miniature electrical storm hovering above.<ref name="Revised and Expanded" /><ref name="Second Edition" />

==History==
===Tirog's visit===
The [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] [[GT-9R]] and his master, a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] named [[Tirog]], visited the cantina to meet with a [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] contact. When they arrived, the Devaronian was drinking a glowing red drink with what appeared to be a small electrical storm hovering overhead. Among the scores of other customers at the time were a group of Human smugglers or traders with a [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] companion, three [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] arguing over a game of [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]], and a very intoxicated [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorrean]] cursing in [[Gamorrese]] and punching the air.<ref name="Second Edition" />

===Thannik's visit===
{{Quote|What a rough place. No one respectable would be found here.''"<br />"''Look, Niner, this is my kind of place. A good bar fight waiting to happen!|GT-9R and Thannik|<ref name="Revised and Expanded" />}}
<!-- Not a duplicate quote, but identical dialogue spoken on two separate occasions. -->

GT-9R also visited the Dancing Dewback with another bounty hunter named [[Thannik]], the outlaw [[Dirk Harkness]], a [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] named [[Rhen]], and a child named [[Cev Rees]]. When this group visited the cantina, it was less crowded, with about fifteen customers present. The purpose of this visit was also to meet with a Devaronian, who was also seen with a glowing red drink. A group of Human smugglers, their Wookiee companion, a trio of Duros gamblers, and a drunken Gamorrean were also present in the Dancing Dewback at this time.<ref name="Revised and Expanded" />

During this visit, Cev Rees picked the pocket of [[Fenn (spacer)|Fenn]], one of the spacers at the bar. When Fenn noticed his wallet was missing, he found Rhen holding it as Rees melted into the crowd. Rhen claimed he had dropped it, and offered the burly spacer a drink in order to avoid any possible confrontation.<ref name="Revised and Expanded" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Dancing Dewback is used in examples of gameplay in the roleplaying game rulebooks ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition]]'' and ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''. The gameplay example describing the Dancing Dewback in the revised rulebook is an expanded version of the one in the previous book, with Tirog replaced by Thannik and with the addition of Dirk Harkness, Rhen, and Cev Rees.

No information is given which can determine a chronology for GT-9R's two visits, or show if the background characters seen during Tirog's visit can be considered the same as those during Thannik's.
